name: Trevor Huval
headline: Full-stack software engineer building production web applications in .NET, React, and SQL.
bio: I'm a software engineer at LSU, where most of my work is replacing systems the university has been running on for decades. It's rarely greenfield — there's usually a mainframe, a PHP app, or a vendor product on the other side of it, and thousands of people depending on the thing while it gets swapped out.

The constraint is what I like about it. Retiring something people use every day means the cutover matters as much as the code: a parallel run to fall back to, a schema that still makes sense in five years, tests that catch the regression before a registrar does. I reach for C# and .NET first, Postgres or SQL Server underneath, and TypeScript wherever a browser is involved.

Outside of work I build things I actually want to use — a query language for playlists, a finance app I self-host, somewhere to rate albums — and I travel with a camera whenever I get the chance. The gallery is the honest version of that one.
